notes:
Below are notes for Mark 9:1–25, with the source URL after each point. One caveat first: my research coverage was thin for vv. 20–25, I found no Catholic-site (newadvent/catholic.com) material, and I found nothing on prosperity or word-of-faith readings of v. 23. Those gaps are left blank rather than filled in.

**v. 1**
- **Context:** Ellicott thinks the chapter break is in the wrong place. He says the verse ought to come, as in St. Matthew and St. Luke, in immediate connection with the foregoing discourse, and calls linking it to the Transfiguration at least a doubtful interpretation. https://biblehub.com/mark/9-1.htm
- **The Transfiguration reading (most common):** Hiebert, quoted at Precept Austin, judges that the primary reference was to the transfiguration serving as a visible type of the eschatological coming of the kingdom. This interpretation was accepted by most of the church Fathers. https://www.preceptaustin.org/mark-9-commentary
- **Several events together:** Cambridge Bible lists the Transfiguration, the resurrection and John living past the fall of Jerusalem. On each of these occasions "the kingdom of God" came "with power." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mark/9-1.htm
- **The Greek:** Ellicott says the verb means they would see the kingdom not "coming," but as having actually come in its completeness. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/mark/9-1.htm
- **Pulpit Commentary:** The Transfiguration fulfils the words only partly. The fall of Jerusalem is also in view. Pulpit credits this view to St. Hilary, St. Chrysostom, St. Ambrose, and others. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm
- **Where traditions differ:**
  - *Reformed:* Ligonier reports that Sproul, in his commentary Mark, argues that Jesus was most likely referring to the destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/witnesses-kingdom
  - *Lutheran:* Lenski says some in the crowd would see the beginning of the final judgment before they died. https://www.preceptaustin.org/mark-9-commentary
  - *Restoration movement:* Coffman says its preachers have long held Mark 9:1 to be a prophecy of the establishment of the church on the first Pentecost. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/mark-9.html
  - *Calvary Chapel:* Chuck Smith suggests the three disciples were taken into a kind of "time chamber" and saw Christ's future glory. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/9-1.html
- **Modern scholarship (NET note):** Lists four options: the Transfiguration, the resurrection and ascension, the coming of the Spirit, and the second coming. It leans to the Transfiguration, although this interpretation is not without its problems. https://classic.net.bible.org/verse.php?book=Mar&chapter=9&verse=1

**v. 2**
- **"Six days" vs. Luke's "eight days":** Pulpit sees no contradiction, because there were six whole days that intervened. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm
- **Why these three:** Pulpit says Jesus showed his glory to Peter, James and John because he would later let them see his agony in the garden. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm
- **Which mountain:** Pulpit rejects the tradition of Mount Tabor. Jesus was near Caesarea Philippi, and Tabor probably had a fortress on top, so it favours Mount Hermon. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm The OCA keeps Tabor by tradition. https://www.oca.org/orthodoxy/the-orthodox-faith/worship/the-church-year/transfiguration
- **"Transfigured":** Guzik quotes Wiersbe: it was a change on the outside that comes from the inside. Spurgeon adds that the real miracle was Jesus usually *hiding* his glory. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/
- **Orthodox view:** The OCA teaches the light was the Light of the Divine Nature, and as such, it was Uncreated and Divine. https://www.oca.org/saints/all-lives/1000/08/06 Christ was not taking upon Himself something new. He was opening the disciples' eyes. https://www.oca.org/fs/sermons/sermon-on-the-transfiguration The feast also shows the perfect image of humanity transfigured by the glory of God. https://www.oca.org/reflections/fr.-steven-kostoff/a-feast-of-divine-beauty

**v. 3**
- **The launderer:** Pulpit says the brightness was in Christ himself and spread to his clothes. A fuller restores soiled cloth, so Mark uses an earthly trade to picture heavenly purity, possibly a detail supplied by Peter. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm

**v. 4**
- **Law and Prophets:** Moses stands for the Law and Elijah for the Prophets. Together they witness to Christ and then resign their offices to him. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm
- **The dead and the living:** Moses died and Elijah was taken up alive. They picture the dead saints and those alive at Christ's return. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm (Guzik says the same.) https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/
- **Futurist view (Guzik):** The two men are likely connected to the witnesses of Revelation 11:3-13. The disciples recognising them suggests we will know one another in heaven. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/

**v. 5**
- **Peter's mistake:** Guzik says the three shelters put Jesus on the same level as Moses and Elijah. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/
- **"Good":** Pulpit notes the Greek means good as in pleasant (*kalon*), not morally good. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/mark-9.html
- **Gracious and Henry:** Pulpit quotes Theophylact: Christians in this life should keep moving forward rather than stay in one place. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm Matthew Henry: if it is good to be with Christ on a mountain, how much better in heaven. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Mar/Mar_009.cfm

**v. 6**
- Pulpit: awe and terror outweighed the joy of the scene. Every revelation of the other world strikes fear. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm
- Guzik: we say foolish things when we speak out of fear. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/

**v. 7**
- **The cloud:** Guzik identifies it as the Shekinah glory-cloud and traces it from the Exodus pillar to the ascension. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/ Pulpit adds that the cloud both showed God's glory and veiled it. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm
- **"Listen to him":** Pulpit reads this as signalling the end of the old order. Listen to Christ, not Moses-style, as the new lawgiver. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm

**v. 8**
- Henry: Christ doth not leave the soul, when extraordinary joys and comforts leave it. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Mar/Mar_009.cfm
- Pulpit: Mark implies the touch of Jesus that Matthew records. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm

**v. 9**
- Pulpit: the resurrection would be the right time to tell, because the Transfiguration was a type of it. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm
- Orthodox (OCA): the apostles saw him risen ahead of time, so their report would only make sense after the Passion. https://www.oca.org/reflections/metropolitan-tikhon/homily-on-the-feast-of-the-transfiguration

**v. 10**
- Pulpit: the disciples already believed in a general resurrection at the end of time. What puzzled them was Jesus' own rising, which he said was close. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm

**vv. 11–13**
- **The Elijah question:** It rests on Malachi 4:5–6. Elijah has come in John the Baptist, though John was not a reincarnation of Elijah. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/
- **Different views of a future Elijah:**
  - Guzik (Calvary Chapel) ties the prophecy mainly to the second coming and the two witnesses of Revelation 11. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/
  - Pulpit says it seems safest to confess our ignorance and the prophecy was partly fulfilled in John. It also cites Augustine and a host of ancient Christian expositors who expected Elijah in person, to convert the Jews. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm
- **v. 12:** Guzik: Jesus points the disciples to the prophecies of his suffering, not only his glory. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/

**v. 14**
- Pulpit notes the Revisers' reading "*they* came," meaning Jesus and the three. Luke's "next day" suggests the Transfiguration happened at night. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm
- Guzik: the scribes were probably criticising the disciples' failure, and this was the kind of conflict Peter hoped to avoid by staying on the mountain. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/

**v. 15 (commentators disagree)**
- Pulpit: the crowd may have seen some traces of the glory of his transfiguration, like Moses' shining face. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/mark/9.htm
- Barclay rejects this. He says a lingering glow would have been to undo his own instructions that it be kept as yet a secret. https://studylight.org/commentaries/dsb/mark-9.html
- Spurgeon (via Precept Austin): Moses' glory pushed people away, but the greater glory of Jesus attracts. https://www.preceptaustin.org/mark-9-commentary

**vv. 16–18**
- Guzik quotes G. Campbell Morgan: Jesus silenced the scribes, comforted the father, healed the boy and taught the disciples. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/
- **"Mute spirit":** Jewish exorcists thought you needed a demon's name to expel it, so a spirit that made someone mute was seen as almost impossible to cast out. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/
- **Epilepsy or a demon?** Guzik grants the signs look like epilepsy but holds that Jesus saw a demon behind them. He quotes Robertson that Jesus was merely indulging popular belief is hard to believe. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/
- **Why the disciples failed:** Jesus had given them authority (Mark 6:7), but some demons may be stronger than others (Ephesians 6:12). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/
- Precept Austin contrasts the perfect Son on the mountain with the tormented son below. https://www.preceptaustin.org/mark-9-commentary

**v. 19**
- "Faithless generation" could mean the scribes, the father or the disciples. Guzik leaves it open. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/

**vv. 20–25**
- I found little verse-specific material.
- **Faith (v. 23):** Kelly says Jesus lets the man see that all turns on faith, and that faith in Christ defeats the enemy's power. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/mark/9-1.html
- **The command to the spirit (v. 25):** Guzik and Robertson note elsewhere that Jesus speaks to the demon as a being separate from the boy. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/mark-9/

**What I didn't find:** No differences between denominations on vv. 21–25, no Catholic sources, and no prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace readings of "all things are possible."
